record.original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. What formula governs T112(3n+1, 3n+1) for n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
With T (n) = T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1) with n >= 1, it appears that T (n) has no prime factor greater than or equal to 4n.
Problem 9: Find a formula governing T112 (3n + 1, 3n + 1). See OEIS entry A364481.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular lattice in the plane. For positive integers $a,b$, the $(a,b)$-benzel is a certain hexagonally-symmetric region in this lattice (a hexagonal analogue of the Aztec diamond) obtained by intersecting three half-planes whose boundaries depend on $a$ and $b$. Two kinds of prototiles are considered:
- "Stones": rhombi formed from two adjacent unit triangles. In the triangular lattice there are two orientations of stones, called the "left stone" and the "right stone".
- "Bones" (tribones): tiles formed from three unit rhombi arranged linearly. There are three possible orientations of bones in the triangular lattice.

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel whose allowed prototiles include the right stone iff $i=1$, include the left stone iff $j=1$, and include exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations (any $k$-element subset, fixed appropriately so that the count is well-defined by the hexagonal symmetry).

Find an explicit closed-form formula for
$$T(n) \;=\; T_{112}(3n+1,\,3n+1), \qquad n\ge 1,$$
the number of tilings of the $(3n+1,3n+1)$-benzel when both stone orientations and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed.
